reviews_1s:
UPDATED: I thought it was just the lids, but it’s both the them and the jars that are a problem! They are not manufactured consistently for precision. This jar set caused me to lose half a batch of jam. I have been making jam for over 30 years and can tell you that it was not operator error. I cranked the lids tighter than normal since they’re one piece instead of cap/band combos. I always turn the jars upside down for the water bath. Five minutes in, there was jam floating in the water and when I lifted a jar out, the lid had completely migrated off, so all the remaining jam dumped out. Never imagining that more than one jar would do this, it happened a second time. You can imagine what a sticky, wasteful, expensive (5 cups of raspberries alone) and aggravating mess this made. I was able to take remaining jars out and salvage some jam (hopefully), but water had seeped into all of them. After cleaning things up, I cranked the lids down as tight as I could and put them in a fresh water bath, upright. By the time it started boiling, I could see air bubbles coming out of some jars. I finally ended up finding spare 2- piece lids in my supplies to rescue a few and refrigerating the remaining four. I tried another batch using name brand two piece lids on these jars: Some sealed and some didn’t.

I like the shape of the jars, the smooth sides and the cute labels. These would be fine for things that don’t need to be sealed, but should absolutely not be advertised or used for canning of any kind.I have ordered these jars several times for my candles. However, the last two orders had many jars with cracks and chips around the seams on the bottom of the jars. These were unsafe to use. I will not buy again.These jars were used for making my candles and some of them broke while lit.
Canning jars should not break!
I will not buy these again.I bought two cases of these jars with the intent to use them for canning tomato sauce. Had everything ready to go, sauce hot, jars washed and sterilized, and at that point discovered that US standard rings (Ball, Kerr, etc.) do NOT fit the threads on the glass of 1/3 to 1/2 of the jars. That means those jars are single use, since I wouldn't trust that any replacement covers would fit either. Buyer beware... Stick with the name brands. You might pay more, but you'll get a quality, truly re-useable product. Naturally I bought them very early to have ready when I needed them, so the option to return them has long since passed...I bought 2 cases of these jars. About 50% of the lids do not screw down tight and pop off, making completely useless. They look cute but not functional!
UPDATE: This is definitely a lesson learned. Just imagine getting up early on the weekend to prepare jams for holiday gifts -- 60 jars are nicely filled and you're almost finished, going down the rows to screw on the lids and HALF of them don't work. It's too late get new lids shipped to you and the first response from customer service is for your to SHIP the defective jars (mind you, now already filled with food) back for a return. Although I realize the customer service agents follow a script, it took 45 minutes for them to agree to just give me a refund for 1 of the 2 boxes (I'm reasonable, 50% of them DID work) instead of asking me to take the time ship back dirty jars. Just buy the Ball jars. Styling is different but those are 100% functional.I was using these jars for homemade jelly and the lids would leak or come off. This didn't happen every time, but you never knew when it was going to happen. When I went to turn the jars upright, the lids would sometime just come off and some time it would just leak around the lids but not coming off. Either way, jelly was everywhere. Needless to say, I had a huge mess in my kitchen. I burned my hand with the hot jelly, not bad, but bad enough. I tried using Ball lids.... that was better, but I still had a few problems of leaking around the lids. I will never use jars that are not name brand again. I should have taken the review telling of this problem to heart, but I had never heard of this problem before and didn't think too much about. Well it definitely is a problem!!!!! If not using to canning, I think these might be just fine.If you need cute jars for an event these are great, I however wanted cute jars for canning and I lost two batches and a lot of hard work when the lids popped off in the canner. Nothing breaks your heart quite like seeing all your hard work floating around in a watery mess. Product says suitable for canning. Lies. Very sad.We purchased two packages of these for canning for about $60. The conclusion is that these jars are worthless!!! We washed all of the bottles, and prepared the jars with jam. We couldn't get the included lids to even screw on the jars, the ones that did we put in the canner. All of the lids popped off not more than 5 minutes into the process. Jam and effort wasted. We tried another batch with regular lids and rings, and the rings didn't grab well on most of them. The result of all of our time is 7 out of 30 that sealed. I want my money back, but all of them are dirty and used at this point. What a waste of money! STAY AWAY FROM THESE ONES!!!These jars are just the perfect size for jams, jellies, and preserves. They; however, do not seal properly. I have had to purchase lids and rings to replace the lids that came with the jars. I lost 36 jars of products canned in the jars because they didn't seal. From the 2nd box of jars after they didn't seal I put new lids and rings on and reprocessed to save product and hard work. Very dissatisfied. I ordered these twice and lost the product in the first box of jars. I went back and checked the seals after the 2nd box didn't seal and had to discard my jellies from the first box of jars as it was too late to reprocess and save the product in the first jars.TERRIBLE!
Probably would be good to mention the lids are not the normal two piece ring and lid. I would not have purchased had I known. I was desperate so I used a couple with the one piece lid and tried several different ring lid combos before I could get them tighten enough not to pop off jars as soon as they met the hot water bath, extremely frustrating! Some jars broke! This is an absolutely terrible pr oduct
